([[Olney, Maryland]]) | college = [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale]] (2021–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = 2025 | years1 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team1 = [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] | years2 = {{nbay|2025|end}} | team2 = [[Utah Jazz]] | highlights = * [[Ivy League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Ivy League Player of the Year]] (2025) * First-team All-[[Ivy League]] (2025) * Second-team All-Ivy League (2024) * 3× Ivy League Defensive Player of the Year (2023–2025) }} '''Bez Mbeng''' (born May 2, 2003) is an American [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Utah Jazz]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale Bulldogs]]. == High school career == Mbeng played at [[Our Lady of Good Counsel High School (Maryland)|Our Lady of Good Counsel High School]] and was coached by GJ Kissal. He was named to the first team All-Washington Catholic Athletic Conference as a junior. Mbeng committed to play college basketball at [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale]] over [[Harvard Crimson men's basketball|Harvard]], despite receiving several scholarship offers.{{cite news |last1=Simms |first1=Brandy |title=Good Counsel's Bez Mbeng will lead Yale on another NCAA Tournament run |url=https://www.si.com/high-school/maryland/good-counsel-s-bez-mbeng-will-lead-yale-on-another-ncaa-tournament-run-01jpq2f8n16t |access-date=March 21, 2025 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=March 19, 2025}} == College career == Mbeng came off the bench as a freshman at Yale. He averaged 10.4 points, 4.2 rebounds, and 3.2 assists per game as a sophomore.{{cite news |last1=Meehan |first1=Jim |title=Short-handed Gonzaga faces challenging opener versus Ivy League favorite Yale |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2023/nov/09/short-handed-gonzaga-faces-challenging-opener-vers/ |access-date=March 21, 2025 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |date=November 9, 2023}} Mbeng was named [[Ivy League]] Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite press release|url=https://ivyleague.com/news/2023/3/7/ivy-league-announces-mens-basketball-major-awards-and-all-ivy-teams.aspx|title=Ivy League Announces Men's Basketball Major Awards and All-Ivy Teams|publisher=Ivy League |date=March 7, 2023 |access-date=March 7, 2023}} As a junior, he averaged 11.1 points, 4.2 rebounds, 4.1 assists, and 1.9 steals per game.{{cite web |title=#135 Yale Men's Basketball 2024-2025 Preview |url=https://www.collegesportsmadness.com/article/22943 |website=College Sports Madness |access-date=March 21, 2025 |date=June 23, 2024}} Mbeng was named to the Second Team All-Ivy League as well as repeating as defensive player of the year.{{cite web |url= https://ivyleague.com/news/2024/3/13/ivy-league-announces-mens-basketball-major-awards-and-all-ivy-teams.aspx |title=Ivy League Announces Men's Basketball Major Awards and All-Ivy Teams|date=March 13, 2024 |website=ivyleague.com |publisher=[[Ivy League]] |access-date=March 13, 2024}} On February 8, 2025, he recorded the second triple-double in program history with 15 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds in a 103–88 win over [[Cornell Big Red men's basketball|Cornell]].{{cite web |title=Mbeng Records Second Triple-Double in Program History; Bulldogs Defeat Cornell |url=https://yalebulldogs.com/news/2025/2/8/mens-basketball-mbeng-records-second-triple-double-in-program-history-bulldogs-defeat-cornell.aspx |website=[[Yale Bulldogs]] |access-date=March 21, 2025 |date=February 8, 2025}} Mbeng was named [[Ivy League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Ivy League Player of the Year]], Ivy League Defensive Player of the Year as well as First Team All-Ivy League.{{cite press release |title=Ivy League Announces Men’s Basketball Major Awards and All-Ivy Teams |url=https://ivyleague.com/news/2025/3/12/ivy-league-announces-mens-basketball-major-awards-and-all-ivy-teams.aspx |publisher=Ivy League |access-date=March 13, 2025 |language=en |date=March 12, 2025}} ==Professional career== On March 13, 2026, Mbeng signed a 10-day contract with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{Cite web|title=Utah Jazz Sign Bez Mbeng to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-bez-mbeng-to-10-day-contract|access-date=March 13, 2026|website=[[nba.com]]|language=en}} Immediately after his signing, Mbeng made his debut with the team, getting four points, rebounds, and assists in 34 minutes of play time in a 114-124 loss against the [[2025–26 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]]. On March 21, Mbeng made his first start for the Jazz against the [[2025–26 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]], where he scored 13 points, grabbed six rebounds, and dished out seven assists in 45 minutes of play time.{{cite web |title=Jazz's Bez Mbeng drawing first career start |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-bez-mbeng-drawing-first-career-start/ |website=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=April 13, 2026 }} After appearing in five games, averaging 4.8 points, 4.2 assists, 4.0 rebounds, and 1.6 steals in 33.4 minutes per game, the Jazz signed Mbeng to a second 10-day contract on March 23.{{cite web |title=Utah Jazz sign Bez Mbeng to second 10-day contract|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-bez-mbeng-to-second-10-day-contract |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=April 13, 2026 }} On April 10, Mbeng recorded a triple-double with a career-high 27 points, 11 rebounds, and 11 assists off the bench in a 147–101 win over the [[2025–26 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]]. His teammate, [[John Konchar]], also recorded a triple-double with 11 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists off the bench, making Mbeng and Konchar the first pair of teammates to each record a triple-double off the bench in a game in NBA history.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/utah-jazz/jazz-news-the-insane-triple-double-history-made-in-tank-off-vs-grizzlies|title=The insane triple-double history made in egregious tank-off Jazz vs. Grizzlies|website=ClutchPoints|last=Ojeda|first=Julian|date=April 11, 2026|access-date=April 11, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401811036|title=Hinson scores a career-high 30 as the Jazz snap a 10-game skid with win over the Grizzlies|work=ESPN.com|date=April 11, 2026|access-date=April 11, 2026}} After his performances with the team, The Jazz later signed Mbeng to a two-year contract on April 3, clearing the way for him to also play in the 2026 [[NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |last=Koch |first=Jared |date=April 2, 2026 |title=Utah Jazz sign Bez Mbeng for rest of season: What it means |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nba/utah-jazz-sign-bez-mbeng-for-rest-of-season-what-it-means/ar-AA200DpD |access-date=April 13, 2026 |website=[[MSN]]}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player
